text:
maria: quick question — i'm templating a helm chart and have two related issues: runtimeClassName should fall back to a cluster default if .Values.node.runtimeClassName is empty, and we also have an optional SENTRY secret. if the secret name is null the rendered manifest blows up. what's the clean pattern folks use for: 1) runtimeClassName fallback, 2) env var precedence (explicit value -> secret -> omit), and 3) avoid chart failure when secretName is nil?

ajay: for runtimeClassName i usually do a default call: `runtimeClassName: {{ default \"cluster-default\" .Values.node.runtimeClassName }}` — simple and explicit.

maria: cool. i tried that but worried about some clusters relying on an empty string vs not set. default handles empty, right?

ajay: default treats empty/zero as missing, yup. if you need to distinguish empty string vs nil you'd have to explicitly check but 99% we just default.

sylvia: for the SENTRY_DSN pattern i use a small helper that prefers an explicit value, then secretKeyRef if secret exists, otherwise we omit the env var entirely. e.g.

```yaml
{{- /* values.sentry: { dsn: "", secretName: "" } */ -}}
env:
  - name: SENTRY_DSN
    {{- if .Values.sentry.dsn }}
    value: {{ .Values.sentry.dsn | quote }}
    {{- else if .Values.sentry.secretName }}
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: {{ .Values.sentry.secretName | quote }}
        key: dsn
    {{- else }}
    # omitted - no env var set when neither value nor secret provided
    {{- end }}
```

that avoids rendering a secretKeyRef with a null name.

maria: nice — i like that explicit branch. any tips to detect secret existence at template render time instead of trusting values?

ajay: helm's `lookup` can help if you want runtime presence check (helm 3+):

```gotmpl
{{- $sec := lookup \"v1\" \"Secret\" .Release.Namespace .Values.sentry.secretName -}}
{{- if $sec }}
# secret exists, render valueFrom...
{{- end }}
```

but remember lookup hits the API server so it's only available during `helm install/upgrade` and may add coupling. for most charts we gate on value presence, not actual k8s objects.

trent: fwiw we had a bug where .Values.sentry.secretName was defined but empty string from an umbrella values merge. defensive check i use: `if and .Values.sentry.secretName (ne .Values.sentry.secretName "")`

sylvia: another option is to allow chart users to explicitly set `sentry.enabled: false` for non-prod. that makes intent clearer than relying on missing strings.

maria: that makes sense — we'll add `.Values.sentry.enabled` toggle and the conditional env snippet. also adding a note in values.yaml that secretName can be omitted.

ajay: small nit — if you want to fail fast for missing required secret in prod use `required` helper at the top of templates: `{{ required \"sentry.dsn is required for production\" .Values.sentry.dsn }}`. only enable that guard via a values flag (e.g., `.Values.sentry.requireInProd`).

maria: perfect. will update the chart with: runtime default, sentry.enabled toggle, explicit branches, optional lookup comment, and a doc blurb. i'll push a PR in a bit — ping me for reviews.

deploy-bot: deploy v1.14.2-staging finished :white_check_mark: (helm upgrade --install)

trent: @maria nice — when you open the PR can you add a tiny unit test for the template rendering with/without sentry values? quick `helm template` check is fine.

maria: yup will include `helm template --values test/values.no-sentry.yaml` in the PR checks. thanks all :thumbsup:
